title: Relative convex-chain bound for an ordered subgroup
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a totally ordered abelian group [def-trf-totally-ordered-abelian-group] and $H\subseteq\Gamma$ any subgroup, with the induced order. A subgroup $C$ of either ordered group is convex if $a,b\in C$ and $a\le x\le b$ imply $x\in C$. Let $h,e\ge0$ be integers. Suppose every finite strict chain of convex subgroups of $H$ has at most $h$ strict inclusions, and $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma/H)\le e$, where $\Gamma/H$ is the quotient abelian group, without any quotient-order requirement, and rational rank means $\dim_{\mathbf Q}((\Gamma/H)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q)$ [def-trf-rational-rank]. Then every finite strict chain of convex subgroups of $\Gamma$ has at most $h+e$ strict inclusions.

proof.text: Fix a finite strict chain $C_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq C_n$ of convex subgroups of $\Gamma$. For $0\le i\le n$ put $D_i=C_i\cap H$, viewed as a subgroup of $H$. If $a,b\in D_i$ and $x\in H$ satisfies $a\le x\le b$, convexity in $\Gamma$ puts $x\in C_i$, hence $x\in D_i$. Thus each $D_i$ is convex in $H$. Let $J=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:D_{i-1}\subsetneq D_i\}$ and let $I$ be its complement. Deleting repeated consecutive terms from the increasing sequence $D_0,\ldots,D_n$ leaves exactly $|J|$ strict inclusions, so $|J|\le h$. If $n=0$ the conclusion already holds.

source.place: Agent-supplied relative chain refinement in the Temkin height-bound branch of (1)--(2); intersection and finite counting argument.

proof.text: For each $i\in I$ choose $x_i\in C_i\setminus C_{i-1}$ and replace it by its negative if necessary so that $x_i>0$. This replacement preserves nonmembership because $C_{i-1}$ is a subgroup. Convexity gives the following observation used below: if $m>0$ is an integer and $m x_i\in C_{i-1}$, then $0\le x_i\le m x_i$ and $0,m x_i\in C_{i-1}$ imply $x_i\in C_{i-1}$, a contradiction.

source.place: Agent-supplied ordered-group argument underlying the relative rational-rank contribution; compare Temkin Section 2.1, printed pp. 7--8.

proof.text: Put $G=\Gamma/H$ as an abelian group and $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, with $j:G\to V$, $j(g)=g\otimes1$. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-tensor-fractions] to $M=G$ with $a=g$ and $b=0$: since $j(0)=0$, $j(g)=0$ holds if and only if $cg=c\cdot0=0$ for some integer $c>0$. Thus $g\otimes1=0$ implies $mg=0$ for some positive integer $m$. No torsion-free hypothesis on $G$ is used; $G$ may have torsion (e.g. $\Gamma=\mathbf Z$, $H=2\mathbf Z$).

proof.text: For $i\in I$ set $v_i=(x_i+H)\otimes1\in V$. We prove these vectors independent. Suppose $\sum_{i\in I}q_i v_i=0$. Write each $q_i=b_i/d_i$ with $b_i\in\mathbf Z$ and positive integer $d_i$, put $d=\prod_{i\in I}d_i$ (empty product $1$), and set $a_i=b_i\prod_{k\in I,\,k\ne i}d_k\in\mathbf Z$. Multiplication of the relation by $d$ and tensor bilinearity give $(\sum a_i(x_i+H))\otimes1=0$. Step 3 supplies $m>0$ with $\sum m a_i x_i\in H$. If some $a_i\ne0$, choose the largest such index $j$. The sum belongs to $C_j$, because $x_i\in C_i\subseteq C_j$ for $i\le j$. Since $j\in I$, it therefore lies in $C_j\cap H=D_j=D_{j-1}\subseteq C_{j-1}$. All terms with $i<j$ already lie in $C_{j-1}$; subtracting them yields $m a_jx_j\in C_{j-1}$. Negating if needed yields $m|a_j|x_j\in C_{j-1}$, contrary to Step 2. Thus every $a_i=0$, and $a_i=dq_i$ with $d>0$ implies every $q_i=0$.

source.place: Agent-supplied largest-index argument for the relative chain bound; denominator and torsion multipliers written explicitly.

proof.text: Enumerate the finite set $I$ by $\mathrm{Fin}\,|I|$. Step 4 and [lem-trf-independent-family-cardinal-dimension] give $|I|\le\dim_{\mathbf Q}V=\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma/H)\le e$, with finite cardinalities interpreted as natural numbers. This uses cardinal dimension and requires no separate finite-dimensionality assumption on $H\otimes\mathbf Q$ or $\Gamma\otimes\mathbf Q$. Finally $I$ and $J$ partition the $n$ inclusions, so $n=|J|+|I|\le h+e$. The chain was arbitrary, which proves the assertion.
